summary: San Bruno sits directly atop the spine of the Peninsula hills yet somehow houses YouTube's global headquarters — a fact that surprises people who picture it as just another BART stop between SFO and downtown San Francisco. That proximity to the airport, combined with a SamTrans bus network and the BART station on Huntington Avenue, makes it a genuine transit node rather than a cul-de-sac suburb, and the Shops at Tanforan mall anchors a commercial corridor that keeps daily errands local. The terrain rises steeply west of El Camino Real toward San Bruno Mountain State Park, whose 12-mile trail network delivers unobstructed bay panoramas — rare for a city only 5.5 square miles in size. At a median household income of roughly $136,000, the home-price-to-income ratio lands near 8.8×, which means purchasing requires substantial down payments or dual incomes even at the median; renting at $2,696 monthly, by contrast, consumes about 24% of gross median income — tight but not crushing. Daily highs average a remarkably stable 64°F year-round with over eight hours of sunshine, though coastal fog regularly spills over the ridgeline and drops evening temperatures into the low 50s. The 5.1% poverty rate and zero recorded homicides in the dataset suggest economic stability, while property crime at roughly 1,995 per 100,000 — driven largely by larceny — tracks with its role as a retail and transit corridor. San Bruno is ultimately a place where a major tech campus, an international airport, and a wildflower-covered mountain coexist within a ten-minute drive of each other, and the tradeoff is that none of those identities fully wins.
